subject: tech
title: Making Things on a Computer
about: A computer is for making things, not just watching them: a drawing, a typed story, a photo, a recording, a slideshow, using the brush, eraser, fill and undo tools of a drawing app, then saving each creation as its own file and sharing it with family with a grown-up's help (K2-CS-03, K2-DA-01). Giving credit means saying who made a picture or song you used, why that is honest, and putting your own name on what you made yourself (K2-AP-06). Read it together, ideally with a drawing app open so he can try each tool as it comes up.
tip: Open a drawing app together, let him try the brush, eraser, fill and undo, then save it with a name he picks and send it to a relative.

cards.q: A computer is for making things too. Which one can you make on a tablet?
cards.note: You can make drawings, stories, photos, songs and slideshows on a computer.

cards.q: You type a story about a dragon on the tablet. What did you make?
cards.note: Typing words into a writing app makes a story. You are the author!

cards.q: You press the red button and sing into the tablet. What did you make?
cards.note: A recording keeps your voice or song so you can play it again.

cards.q: You point the tablet at your dog and tap the round button. What did you make?
cards.note: The camera turns what it sees into a picture file. You made it by choosing what to snap.

cards.q: You put five photos in a row to show one after another. What is it called?
cards.note: A slideshow shows pictures one at a time. Add words and music to tell a story.

cards.q: In a drawing app, which tool makes a line follow your finger?
cards.note: The brush paints lines. Pick a color and a size, then drag your finger.

cards.q: You drew one line in the wrong spot. Which tool rubs it out?
cards.note: The eraser takes away only where you rub. The rest of the drawing stays.

cards.q: You want the whole sky blue with one tap. Which tool fills a big space fast?
cards.note: The fill tool pours one color into a whole space. One tap and the sky is blue.

cards.q: You tap undo three times. How many of your last lines go away?
cards.note: Each undo takes back one step. Three taps, three steps back.

cards.q: You made a song recording and a drawing. How many files did you make?
cards.note: Each thing you make is saved as its own file: a song file and a picture file.

cards.q: You open your saved drawing and add a sun. What do you do so the sun stays?
cards.note: Saving again keeps the new version. The sun is still there tomorrow.

cards.q: You want Grandma to see your drawing. What is a good way to share it?
cards.note: Sharing what you made with family is great. A grown-up picks the safe way to send it.

cards.q: Saying who made a picture or song you used has a name. What is it?
cards.note: Giving credit is honest. Programmers and artists do it every day.

cards.q: You put a picture from a website in your slideshow. What do you add under it?
cards.note: Write the maker's name under the picture. That is giving credit.

cards.q: Why do we say who made a picture or song we used?
cards.note: The maker worked hard on it, so saying their name is honest and fair. It also lets people find more of their work.

cards.q: You drew the picture all by yourself. Whose name goes under it?
cards.note: You made it, so the credit is yours. Sign your drawings like a real artist.

cards.q: A watcher only watches videos. A maker makes things. Which one are you when you draw on the tablet?
cards.note: Making beats only watching. Your ideas go into the computer and come out as something new.

cards.q: Who can make a drawing, a story or a song on a computer?
cards.note: Kids make real things on computers. You already did: the first drawing you saved.
